questions.questionText: Neither of the two candidates ___ selected for the interview.
questions.explanation: 'Neither' is a singular pronoun, so it takes a singular verb: was.
questions.shortcut: Neither / Each / Either / One of + plural noun takes a singular verb.

questions.questionText: She has been working in this company ___ 2019.
questions.explanation: 'Since' is used with a fixed point in time (2019) with the present perfect continuous; 'for' is used with a period.
questions.shortcut: Point of time -> since; length of time -> for.

questions.questionText: Each of the students ___ given a certificate of merit.
questions.explanation: 'Each' is singular, so the verb is singular: was given.

questions.questionText: If I ___ you, I would accept the offer immediately.
questions.explanation: For an unreal (imaginary) condition in the present, the subjunctive 'were' is used for all persons in standard grammar.

questions.questionText: The news of the victory ___ received with great joy.
questions.explanation: 'News' is an uncountable noun and takes a singular verb.
questions.shortcut: News, furniture, information, advice: always singular.

questions.questionText: By the time we reached the station, the train ___.
questions.explanation: Two past actions: the earlier one (the train leaving) is in the past perfect, the later (our reaching) in the simple past.
questions.shortcut: 'By the time' + simple past -> past perfect in main clause.

questions.questionText: One of my friends ___ a pilot in the Indian Air Force.
questions.explanation: 'One of + plural noun' takes a singular verb because the subject is 'One'.

questions.questionText: The teacher, along with her students, ___ going on a trip to Mysuru.
questions.explanation: 'Along with' does not make the subject plural; the verb agrees with 'The teacher', so it is singular.
questions.shortcut: Along with / together with / as well as: ignore the added noun.

questions.questionText: He suggested that she ___ a doctor immediately.
questions.explanation: After verbs like suggest, insist, recommend and demand, a 'that' clause takes the base form of the verb (subjunctive): see.

questions.questionText: It is high time we ___ the problem seriously.
questions.explanation: 'It is high time' is followed by the simple past (past subjunctive) to show that action is overdue.

questions.questionText: I am looking forward to ___ you at the wedding.
questions.explanation: In 'look forward to', 'to' is a preposition, so the verb that follows takes the -ing form.

questions.questionText: Of the two brothers, Ramesh is the ___.
questions.explanation: When two persons are compared, the comparative degree (taller) is used, not the superlative.
questions.shortcut: Two things -> comparative; three or more -> superlative.

questions.questionText: Hardly had he reached the platform ___ the train started moving.
questions.explanation: 'Hardly' (and 'scarcely') is followed by 'when'; 'than' goes with 'no sooner'.

questions.questionText: No sooner did he enter the hall ___ the lights went out.
questions.explanation: 'No sooner' is correctly followed by 'than'.

questions.questionText: Mathematics ___ my favourite subject since childhood.
questions.explanation: Names of subjects ending in -s (mathematics, physics, economics) are singular; 'since' needs the present perfect: has been.

questions.questionText: The scissors on the table ___ very sharp.
questions.explanation: 'Scissors' is a plural-only noun, so the verb is plural: are.

questions.questionText: I wish I ___ taller so that I could join the police force.
questions.explanation: After 'wish' referring to an unreal present situation, the subjunctive 'were' is used.

questions.questionText: Let us start the work now, ___?
questions.explanation: The question tag for 'Let us ...' is 'shall we'.

questions.questionText: He cannot swim across the river, ___?
questions.explanation: A negative statement takes a positive tag with the same auxiliary: cannot -> can he.

questions.questionText: She ___ her homework when the teacher entered the room.
questions.explanation: A past continuous action is interrupted by a simple past action (entered): was doing.

questions.questionText: Unless you ___ hard, you will not pass the examination.
questions.explanation: 'Unless' already carries a negative meaning, so the verb that follows is affirmative, in the present tense for a future condition.

questions.questionText: The number of students in our college ___ increasing every year.
questions.explanation: 'The number of' takes a singular verb, because the subject is 'number'.
questions.shortcut: The number of -> singular; A number of -> plural.

questions.questionText: A number of students ___ absent from the class today.
questions.explanation: 'A number of' means 'several' and takes a plural verb.

questions.questionText: He speaks as if he ___ the owner of the company.
questions.explanation: 'As if' expressing an unreal comparison takes the subjunctive 'were'.

questions.questionText: The more you practise, ___ you become.
questions.explanation: The structure 'the + comparative ..., the + comparative' needs 'the better'.

questions.questionText: Many a student ___ failed in this examination.
questions.explanation: 'Many a' is followed by a singular noun and a singular verb: has failed.
questions.shortcut: Many a + singular noun + singular verb.

questions.questionText: Either Meena or her cousins ___ coming to the party tonight.
questions.explanation: With 'either ... or', the verb agrees with the nearer subject, 'cousins' (plural): are.
questions.shortcut: Either/Neither ... or/nor: verb agrees with the nearest noun.

questions.questionText: Neither the manager nor his assistants ___ present at the meeting.
questions.explanation: With 'neither ... nor', the verb agrees with the nearer subject, 'assistants', so it is plural: were.

questions.questionText: The doctor suggested ___ to the hills for a few weeks.
questions.explanation: The verb 'suggest' is followed by a gerund (-ing form), not by an infinitive.

questions.questionText: He is used to ___ up early in the morning.
questions.explanation: In 'be used to', 'to' is a preposition, so the -ing form follows.

questions.questionText: The books ___ I bought yesterday are very expensive.
questions.explanation: The relative pronoun for things is 'which'. 'What' cannot follow a noun, 'whom' is for persons and 'whose' shows possession.

questions.questionText: The man ___ car was stolen has lodged a complaint.
questions.explanation: The car belongs to the man, so the possessive relative pronoun 'whose' is required.

questions.questionText: The girl ___ I met at the airport is my cousin.
questions.explanation: 'Whom' is the object form for a person (I met her); 'whose', 'which' and 'what' do not fit.

questions.questionText: I have never seen ___ elephant as tall as that one.
questions.explanation: 'Elephant' begins with a vowel sound, so the article 'an' is used.

questions.questionText: He bought ___ one-rupee coin from the shop.
questions.explanation: 'One' begins with the consonant sound /w/, so the article is 'a', not 'an'.
questions.shortcut: Article depends on sound, not spelling: a one-rupee, a university, an hour.

questions.questionText: If it rains tomorrow, we ___ the picnic.
questions.explanation: A real future condition (present tense in the if-clause) takes 'will' + base verb in the main clause.

questions.questionText: If she had studied harder, she ___ the examination.
questions.explanation: An unreal past condition (had studied) takes 'would have + past participle' in the main clause.
questions.shortcut: If + had + V3, ... would have + V3.

questions.questionText: She said that she ___ the film the previous day.
questions.explanation: In reported speech, a past action that came before the reporting verb is expressed in the past perfect: had seen.
questions.shortcut: Reported speech: simple past -> past perfect.

questions.questionText: I ___ in this city since I was a child.
questions.explanation: 'Since' with a point in the past and an action continuing to now needs the present perfect: have lived.

questions.questionText: Water ___ at 100 degrees Celsius at sea level.
questions.explanation: A scientific fact is expressed in the simple present; 'water' is singular, so boils.

questions.questionText: Of the two plans, this one is ___.
questions.explanation: Comparison of two items uses the comparative with 'the': the better.

questions.questionText: Gulliver's Travels ___ written by Jonathan Swift.
questions.explanation: A title of a book is treated as singular, and the sentence is about a past writing: was.
questions.shortcut: Book / film titles take singular verbs.

questions.questionText: Ten kilometres ___ a long distance to walk every day.
questions.explanation: A distance treated as a single unit takes a singular verb.

questions.questionText: The furniture in the old house ___ been sold.
questions.explanation: 'Furniture' is uncountable and singular, so 'has been' is correct.

questions.questionText: Ravi, as well as his friends, ___ invited to the function.
questions.explanation: 'As well as' does not change the number of the subject; 'Ravi' is singular, so the verb is singular.

questions.questionText: The patient ___ before the doctor arrived at the hospital.
questions.explanation: Two past events: the death happened before the doctor's arrival, so the earlier one takes the past perfect.

questions.questionText: The Principal, as well as the teachers, ___ attending the seminar tomorrow.
questions.explanation: 'As well as' does not make the subject plural; the subject is 'The Principal' (singular).
